Service: SAP Internet Transaction Server (ITS) - Legacy HTTP Ports
Description: Ports such as 3950, 3951, 3954, and 3964 are used by the standalone SAP Internet Transaction Server (ITS) to provide browser-based access to SAP GUI transactions. ITS predates modern ICM-based handling and was designed to render classic SAP Dynpro screens as HTML for delivery over the web.
Deployment Context: ITS was historically deployed either as a standalone component (typically using 395x/396x ports) or integrated into the NetWeaver stack via ICM. The standalone configuration was common in early SAP web environments and still exists in legacy deployments or segmented environments. These interfaces provide users with WebGUI access without requiring the SAP GUI client.
Access Behavior: These ports expose browser-accessible HTTP endpoints for interacting with SAP backend transactions. The ITS server maintains session state and renders HTML views of ABAP screens. Commonly exposed paths include /scripts/wgate/webgui/, /sap/bc/gui/sap/its/webgui, and /sap/public/icmandir/its. Unlike modern ICM, these interfaces are tightly coupled with the legacy ITS runtime.
Functional Capabilities: ITS enables execution of classic SAP GUI transactions within a browser. It supports session management, language selection, and transaction flow similar to the native SAP GUI. While functional, it lacks many of the enhancements found in Fiori or modern ICM-based interfaces, and often relies on older HTML rendering logic.
Security Implications: Legacy ITS deployments can expose login interfaces, transaction forms, and ABAP interactions directly over the web. If left exposed without modern controls (e.g., strong auth, TLS, firewalls), they can be abused for session hijacking, credential harvesting, or backend interaction. The age and architectural limitations of ITS increase its attack surface in unpatched environments.
Detection Goals: This module will identify active ITS deployments by probing known legacy ports and scanning for ITS-specific paths. It will attempt to fingerprint the backend ABAP instance, detect session management behavior, and confirm whether the deployment is standalone or integrated. It may also assess cookie behavior and session persistence.
Assessment Notes: If these legacy ITS ports are open and respond with recognizable WebGUI content, the system likely exposes a standalone ITS instance. This can provide valuable insight into older SAP deployments and should be evaluated for patch level, exposure risk, and potential architectural weaknesses.
